about.title: Personal Injury Help in Anaheim, California
about.longDescription: Anaheim draws millions of visitors to its resort and convention district each year, layering heavy tourist traffic onto a working Orange County city. Public records show more than 2,100 injury collisions in Anaheim in 2025, leaving over 3,100 people hurt, with reported crashes tending to peak on Friday evenings. The SR-91 (Riverside Freeway) and busy arterials like Ball Road and Lincoln Avenue carry a steady mix of commuters, visitors and pedestrians. Whether you were injured in a wreck, in a fall at a hotel or business, in a workplace incident, or by a defective product, California law gives you rights and a limited window to act. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people in Anaheim with an independent personal injury attorney who understands how Orange County claims and courts work. We are not a law firm; we match you with counsel and stay out of your way. You pay no fee unless your case recovers compensation.

whyChoose.title: What Anaheim injury victims should know

items.title: Two-year California deadline
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of injury to file. In a high-traffic tourist area, surveillance and camera footage can be overwritten within days.

items.title: Visitors have rights too
items.desc: You don't have to live in Anaheim to bring a claim for an injury that happened here. California law applies wherever the injury occurred.

items.title: Partial fault won't bar recovery
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so you can recover even if you were partly at fault; your award is reduced by your share.

items.title: No cap on pain and suffering
items.desc: Most California injury cases place no limit on non-economic damages, so the human toll of your injury can be part of your claim.

items: Adjusters or a hotel's insurer calling before you've finished treatment

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Anaheim?
items.answer: Most California injury claims must be filed within two years. Claims against a public entity can carry deadlines as short as six months, so speak with an attorney quickly.

items.question: I was just visiting Anaheim when I got hurt. Can I still file?
items.answer: Yes. California law applies to injuries that happen here regardless of where you live. An attorney can handle the claim even if you've since returned home.

items.question: What if the accident was partly my fault?
items.answer: You can still recover. California's pure comparative fault rule reduces your award by your percentage of fault rather than eliminating it.

items.question: What does a case review cost?
items.answer: Nothing. The review is free and attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no attorney fee unless they recover compensation for you.

items.question: Where do injury crashes cluster in Anaheim?
items.answer: Reported-collision records for recent years point to the SR-91 (Riverside Freeway) and arterials like Ball Road and Lincoln Avenue, with crashes peaking on Friday evenings. These are public-record counts, not a verdict about any road.
